newsitem.title: USA: Supervalu to exit ShopKo stake.
newsitem.headline: Supervalu to exit ShopKo stake.

text.p: ShopKo Stores Inc and SuperValu Inc said they have reached an agreement in which Supervalu Inc will exit its 46 percent investment through a $150 million share buyback and a secondary public offering.

Under the first of the two simultaneous planned transactions, ShopKo said it will repurchase 8.2 million shares of its common stock held by SupervValu for $18.35 per share. The deal represents a $0.65 per share discount from the Aporil 24, 1997 closing price of ShopKo shares.
ShopKo said it will fund the buyback through $125 million in cash and $25 million of short-term bank borrowings.

The second transaction is a secondary public offering of 6.6 million shares of ShopKo common stock, representing the balance of Supervalu's stake in ShopKo. The transactions are conditional on each other. The companies said Supervalu is required to proceed with the secondary offering if the share price to the public in the offering is at or above $18.35.
The two transactions, which are subject to certain other conditions, are expected to close in the summer of 1997.
ShopKo said it may have to take a one-time charge in fiscal 1998 related to the transactions of up to $8.5 million if it is required to pay certain costs associated with the transaction.
Excluding the charge, the transactions are expected to be accretive to earnings.
ShopKo also said it will postpone its annual shareholders meeting until after the Supervalu transaction is completed. It was not immediately known when the meeting had been slated.

Supervalu said it intends to consider a number of options for the proceeds of the transaction and intends to avoid earnings per share dilution. Supervalu chairman Mike Wright said the proceeds may be used to purchase treasury stock, reduce debt or invest via acquisition in the company's core wholesale or retail food operations.

Upon the closing of the transactions, Wright, who had also served as chairman of ShopKo, and Jeff Girard, Supervalu's executive vice president and chief financial officer, will leave the ShopKo board of directors. The companies said it is expected that Dale Kramer will be named chairman of ShopKo, while maintaining his position as president, chief executive officer and director. Bill Podany, chief operating officer of ShopKo Stores, will be nominated as an additional director.
Kramer said the transactions will preserve ShopKo's financial flexibility to grow through acquisitions and make future capital expenditures.
Supervalu previously had announced plans to divest its ShopKo stake. It bought ShopKo in 1971 and then sold 54 percent of its stock in a 1991 public offering.

The two companies were expected to move quickly to provide an exit strategy for Supervalu following the collapse earlier this month of ShopKo's proposed $1 billion merger with Phar-Mor Inc. Although the two companies did not cite the reason for the collapse of their deal, sources familiar with the companies cited a decline in Phar-Mor's stock price, regulatory delays and uncertainty about the position of one large Phar-Mor shareholder.
